score.register_pressure_finding: The retained assembly needs exactly the 7 non-r4 callee-usable registers this compiler's -fcall-used-r4 route allows (r5,r6,r7,r8,r9,sl,fp) for window, menu, visible_count, row, the psynergies cursor, owner, and ability, and it fits them all -- no spill. Every C shape tried for this owner instead has the allocator spill `menu` (struct PsynergyMenuState *, holding Data_03001f2c) to a real stack slot (`sub sp,#8` / `str r3,[sp,#4]` instead of reference's `sub sp,#4` / `mov sl,r3`), which then cascades: with `menu` off the register file, the allocator reassigns the fp/r9/sl roles that reference uses for visible_count/row/menu differently (mine: menu spilled, the 0x3fff mask constant cached in fp instead, row ends up in sl), and that reassignment is visible in every downstream instruction that touches those three roles even though the underlying algorithm is identical. Confirmed directly by compiling the candidate through xgcc -da (GCC 2.96's own RTL dumps, in an ignored out/ directory, per CONTRIBUTING's 'treat the compiler as evidence' guidance): the .18.greg dump lists exactly 10 pseudos needing global allocation, of which pseudo 42 (menu, defined at the *(void**)Data_03001f2c dereference) and pseudo 80 (a cached copy of the 0x3fff mask constant, HImode) are the two that fail to get a hard register ('Spilling for insn 18' is menu's own definition instruction); pseudo 82 (a second, SImode cached copy of the same 0x3fff constant, used by the other two AND sites) does get fp. Reference's own assembly reloads 0x3fff from the literal pool independently at each of its three uses (three different pc-relative offsets reaching the same single pool word) rather than caching it in a register at all, so reference's allocator never has this extra competing pseudo in the first place.
bounded_checks: Baseline draft (typed struct BattleUnit*/BattleAction* pointers, const u16 *psynergy cursor incremented with psynergy++, y=row*16+8 not cached): candidate=368, differing_halfwords=159, wrong_instructions=102 -- the Menu_DrawPageIndicator call passed the already-cached `page`/`first_entry` locals instead of re-reading state->page/state->entry_count the way item_name_page.c's own source does for that specific call (a genuine, evidence-backed redundant-reload idiom, not noise); fixing that alone dropped wrong_instructions to 78 with zero other changes.

From the 78-instruction baseline: hoisting owner/ability declarations to function scope, reordering local declarations (menu first vs last), switching the header-flag read between &menu->owner_ids[6] and a raw (u8*)menu+0x220 cast, switching owner/ability between typed struct pointers and raw u8* with index/offset field access, caching row*16+8 into a named `y` local vs inlining it twice, and marking the psynergy cursor `volatile` (which did change the RTL -- it gave each of the three *psynergy reads its own short-lived pseudo instead of one GCSE'd value, confirmed in the -da dump -- but left wrong_instructions at exactly 78, because the still-cached 0x3fff mask constant was never the volatile-affected value) all measured byte-identical output: exactly 78 wrong_instructions, sub sp,#8, every time. None of these are the lever.

Recomputing the loop body's array access as menu->psynergies[first_entry+row] (indexed by the loop counter, no separate cursor variable) regressed sharply: candidate grew to 380 bytes, differing_halfwords=152 but wrong_instructions=118 -- worse on the metric that matters, because the compiler recomputes the full address (multiply + two adds) every one of three reads per iteration instead of the reference's single +2 increment.

Replacing the pointer-walk cursor with an explicit s32 byte-offset variable (`cursor`, incremented by 2 each iteration) dereferenced through `*(const u16*)((u8*)menu->psynergies + cursor)` at all three read sites -- intended to force the compiler to route each read through 2-register (menu, cursor) addressing the way reference's `ldrh r3,[r6,r2]` does, keeping `menu` 'busy' and therefore high-priority -- gave the best result found: candidate=368, differing_halfwords=160, wrong_instructions=74 (kept; this is the current draft). Inspecting the -da dump afterward showed the hypothesis behind this change was itself wrong (the compiler still pre-combines menu+offset+cursor into one materialized pointer, `[r6,#0]` addressing, same as the plain pointer-walk version) -- the 4-instruction improvement over the 78-instruction baseline is real but not for the reason attempted.

An explicit (s32) cast around each masked read, attempting to force the AND to compute in a single consistent mode (rather than the HImode/SimODE split the -da dump shows for the cached mask constant) and thereby collapse the two competing mask-constant pseudos into one: zero measured effect (still 74/368/160).

Semantic summary: draws one page (up to 5 rows) of the Psynergy-menu entry list into `window`. Commits the window, opens its 11x16 frame, then draws one of two header captions (message 0xae1 or 0xb89) chosen by a bit in a not-yet-named field at Data_03001f2c+0x220. Computes first_entry=state->page*5 and the page's visible row count (state->entry_count-first_entry, clamped to 5), draws the paging strip (Func_080a2324) and page indicator (Menu_DrawPageIndicator), and a static column header (message 0xaed). For each visible row: looks up the current owner's battle record and the row's ability definition, colors the row by PP-affordability then by PsynergyMenu_IsActionRestricted, draws the ability name (message base Value_00000333 + the 14-bit action id) and its PP cost, then resets the palette color before the next row. Always returns 1.

The residual is entirely a register-allocation-level mismatch (menu spilled to the stack vs reference keeping it in sl the whole function, with a cached 0x3fff AND-mask constant occupying the register menu would otherwise use), confirmed against the compiler's own -da RTL dumps rather than guessed at; no further permutation search is justified without a genuinely new lever, per Cleanroom's 'do not spend an open-ended search on a tiny residual' guidance -- though at 74/~150 instructions this is a substantial, not tiny, residual, so a future pass with a different register-pressure lever (not yet tried: shrinking the ability/owner pointer lifetimes, or restructuring the header-caption branch) may still close it.
